newsitem.title: USA: USDA says no change in China corn export policy.
newsitem.headline: USDA says no change in China corn export policy.

text.p: A senior U.S. Agriculture Department official said Tuesday there has been no change in China's corn export policy, and that USDA does not expect Chinese corn exports to resume any time soon.
"Our folks in China are reporting no apparent change in China's (corn) export policy," said Tim Galvin, associate administrator for USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service.
"We don't anticipate any nearterm change in their export policy...We're relatively sure they won't export (corn) in the near term," said Galvin.

Reports circulated last week that the Chinese government was considering relaxing its current ban on corn exports to allow 2.0 million tonnes of corn to be exported from the northeastern province of Jilin -- China's top corn producing region.
USDA officials said at the time they were looking into the reports, but had received no confirmation of a policy change.
Galvin told Reuters that USDA has determined that the reports were triggered by 2.0 million tonnes of corn being moved last week from Jilin into the southeastern areas of the country.
"It was internal movement that people have misinterpreted as exports," Galvin said.
Galvin also pointed out that because Chinese corn is currently priced higher than corn traded on the world market, it would not be a good time to enter the export market.

Grain industry sources said that while China may be holding off on exports for the time being, they still expected China to export corn sometime this marketing year, given the record size of the Chinese corn crop.

"It's almost inevitable that the Chinese, given how big their crop is, will export," said an official with a major exporting company. "But it's also consistent that they haven't exported yet, given the high value of their corn."
